Not for redistribution without written consent of Morgan Stanley Morgan Stanley RESEARCH Idea July 1, 2026 09:45 PM GMT Meta Platforms Inc | North America 5 Takes On The Neocloud vs Hyperscaler Opportunities We remain bullish the neocloud optionality, temporarily monetizing excess capacity in a compute constrained world, and paint multiple paths to $3+ (8%+) of EPS. But building a broader software offering would be challenging, requiring models/ software, personnel, go to market, and likely more capex. What Happened? This morning, Bloomberg reported Meta is developing plans for a cloud business, setting up a potential new competitor with AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. The plans reportedly include two potential offerings: 1) hosted API/modelaccess service similar to AWS Bedrock (which would serve models including Muse Spark to developers) and 2) a neocloud-like raw silicon offering. The effort would sit within Meta Compute, the business division they set up in January to manage the company's compute procurement. Note Meta has not commented on this morning's headlines. 1. Neocloud Option Much Easier than Fuller Service Hyperscaler: In our view, the hosted API/model-access business would have more technology, hiring, and execution risk. Meta's Muse suite of models would also need to improve...consider that their first family of Muse models didn't score well on TerminalBench and SWE Bench Verified (which are important to coding and third party use). Future Muse models would have to improve to compete against Gemini and other frontier models. In addition to being behind on leading models, we don't believe META has the personnel or software offerings to readily compete here, and competing with AWS/Azure/GCP would require salespeople with enterprise go to market expertise. As such, a full API of models and applications would have significantly more execution risk and should be viewed as a "show me" vs. more scaled and established hyperscalers. But the neocloud opportunity would require less hiring and "new muscle" building as we have seen other tech companies sell excess capacity without meaningful hiring/incremental team build. 2. META Seems to have Capacity Coming on to Lease: In 4 Products to Turn Meta Back into an "AI Winner" we detailed the Meta neocloud opportunity and remind investors that we estimate META will bring on ~2 GW / ~3.5 GW incremental owned-operated IT capacity in '26/'27 (on an estimated YE25 base of ~3 GW). Companies are compute constrained and continue to make compute budgeting decisions between training, inference or other products/uses….while also balancing near-term ROIC and long-term opportunities. But as a comparison, we expect hyperscalers like AMZN/GOOGL to add 5 GW/9 GW of IT capacity in '27...which speaks to the theoretical opportunity for Meta to have compute capacity to lease, even if on a temporary basis. Note that while we do not believe META is able to lease its estimated ~2.5 GW it is renting from third parties (like Coreweave, Nebius, GCP, ORCL and others) this capacity does give them more flexibility to rent out its

Neocloud EPS Accretion is Meaningful...Other recent neocloud deals, detailed in GOOGL's $50/Watt Deal and What It Signals for GOOGL, AMZN, META and GenAI ROIC (17 Jun 2026) speak to the growing flexibility neocloud deals are being struck with (smaller sizes, shorter duration, dual-sided opt out clauses, etc). Our sensitivity table below showcases the potential EPS accretion, but for perspective, the EPS upside of monetizing this scarce resource is material….as every 250 MW leased for 1 year at $40/Watt would add ~$3 (8%) to our '28 EPS. Please let us know if interested in our interactive Meta Neocloud model. Exhibit 2: We estimate that every 250 MW leased for 1 year at $40/Watt could generate ~$3 of EPS upside in '28...

But 1P Products/Innovation Still Key to META Multiple: Our OW view on META is not based on it being a neocloud...it is based on the company developing new products for its platforms that drive more durable multi-year engagement and revenue growth. So while monetizing spare compute as a neocloud is a strong potential "EPS bridge" as we await new products to scale, MetaAI, business agents/ messengers, diffusion offerings, subscription revenue streams and others are front and center for us as detailed in 4 Products to Turn Meta Back into an "AI Winner". We look for more evidence of Meta developing and scaling these businesses to drive outperformance and a higher multiple. 5. And What about Capex? Our model currently assumes META capex grows to $175bn/$205bn in '27/'28 (from $145bn in '26) as they bring on ~3.5 GW of capacity in '27. Note our model essentially assumes they are building capacity for their own 1P products but not a full functioning hyperscale business with an API/suite of models and tools. And we assume the neocloud to be a temporary stop gap rather than permanent business to scale. As such, the extent to which META is indeed going to focus on these opportunities (which as detailed above have higher risk) would put upward bias on our '27/'28 capex (in order to build more long-term data center capacity for this new business offering). We look to learn more from the company over time on these key topics. Morgan Stanley Research

View descriptions of Risk Rewards Themes here BULL CASE Implied ~28x '27 P/E $1,000.00 AI investments drive increased engagement and lead to new products/tools, which supports outsized ad monetization and revenue growth. Execution on newer offerings (like click to message) could also contribute to higher than expected growth. META could also drive further ef ciency gains and be more successful in closing the Reels monetization gap. Reality Labs losses fimoderate and macro environment is better than expected. BASE CASE Implied ~23X base case '27 P/E Ad revenue grows ~28% in '26 as META's AI investments drive incremental Reels engagement/monetization and support improved performance and ad measurement/attribution across the Family of Apps. We also see META continuing to focus on ef ciency and improving productivity. $775.00 BEAR CASE $450.00 Implied ~14x '27 P/E Declines in engagement and/or evidence of Reels monetization ramping more slowly than expected could lead to lower growth and greater uncertainty. We also watch for any macro uncertainty, regulation that limits META's ability to target ads, Reality Labs losses widen more materially than expected, and higher capital intensity from misexecution around the data center build. Any additional opex and capex could weigh on operating income growth and FCF. Morgan Stanley Research
